title: Opinion: The future is personalized custom games and not app stores.
author: Only-Cheetah-9579
selftext:
The way things are going, I really think personalized apps and games are going to be the future. Custom tailored experiences for the user. 

Building games to sell to others gonna change big time. 

For single player experiences we can create our own worlds just for ourselves.

With this I see less and less need for app stores and game developers.

The network effects and shared games will stick around but people will gravitate only to AAA games or some very special indie titles ,like they mostly do already, while the smaller publishers will generally be even less successful, just because the lack of network effects won't drive customers who now have the option to have a custom experience tailored to them. 

Same way you can get shoes tailored, you can get games tailored to your specifications. 

Why would you wait for the next episode of your favorite game when you can just generate it?

comments.author: Soft_Product_243
comments.body: I don’t know, boss. I’ve been building my own game for a couple months now, it’s fun to build, it’s fun to play, but the time sink to build a solid experience and achieve a reasonable level of quality it is incredible. What I’m saying is that it’s a lengthy process.

comments.author: curreylabs
comments.body:
Not like that.

It will be a good game that can adjust.

replies.author: wylderzone
replies.body:
You only need to take a look at what is happening in the Valheim mod scene to realise, that even with an amazing base game as a foundation, many people lack any real creativity or understanding of game design.

It is the equivalent of someone copy pasting scenes of The Office into Lord of the Rings.

replies.author: curreylabs
replies.body:
Absolutely most people are not good at designing games. Its hard and takes experience.

Doesn’t mean games wont be highly personalized. You seem to be missing the fact that the good game designers can leverage AI as well. The game could tailor itself.

replies.author: wylderzone
replies.body: Good game designers will be authoring things with intent - not copy pasting skateboarding into call of duty

replies.author: curreylabs
replies.body:
>Good game designers will be authoring things with intent

Yup. Like systems that can adapt to the player.

replies.author: wylderzone
replies.body: Just drop the link for whatever you are trying to sell already

comments.author: Coldfriction
comments.body:
Have you ever noticed how cooking for yourself never tastes quite as good as eating out?  Like food you put zero effort in making or cleaning up somehow tastes better? 

Ever notice how art you make seems to have more flaws than the art other people make?  Like the best you can do seems "off" compared the the art other people put out that you don't see the process of being made?

Ever notice how what etertained you as a kid filled you with more wonder than what etertains you as an adult?  Like the games and movies are better made and dramatically improved in every way but the stuff from your childhood made you so much more entertained?

Here's the thing about being in total control, it sucks for entertainment.  It sucks for perception.  Good games are about constraints and restrictions, challenges, and experiences.  People will always prefer to experience the creations of others over their own.  The best games won't ever have too much user control of their creation.

Sure AI can make a custom tailored game but now how do you talk about to.your friends at school?  How do you share with an online community about it?  What anticipation is there to share with others for the next installment?

I see things being as they are with higher quality and a LOT of failure and some games succeeding where the rest fail.

Still waiting for flying cars I was told would be here two decades ago.

I agree that indies will have a bad future unless they move up the chain to be more like AAA games.

replies.author: Only-Cheetah-9579
replies.body: You lost me at the first line. I am an excellent cook and prefer to cook over eating out

replies.author: Coldfriction
replies.body: All things being equal, people judge food to be better that they don't prepare themselves.  There are studies on this.  You anecdotal experience is not how you make decisions to market to other people who aren't you.  If your game dev is only for yourself, then fine your annedoct is relevant.

replies.author: Only-Cheetah-9579
replies.body:
yes but AI is an excellent game dev and it's just gonna get better.

You are not building games completely yourself, they are created for you. 

Like a 5 star restaurant, you make your order, the game is cookin and you get a special meal just for you.

replies.author: Coldfriction
replies.body:
Sure, but you are going to a restaurant for their food and not cooking your own.  You recognize that the restaurant makes delicious stuff and when you go there you get to share the experience with someone (eating alone isn't really common).  Someone else is cheating the meals served.

AI is going to make this dramatically more customizable, but I still think most people want a console like experience without thinking about it.  Most PC gamers don't want to dig into the config files so to speak either.

There will be a niche group that want games ultra customized to themselves too, but it won't be the majority in my opinion.

There are a lot of possibilities out there, but a game dev that wants others to experience their games needs to understand the market and how people work.  People want simple and convenient and game devs are often detailed and complex in their thinking.

EVERY game dev thinks about how the game could be better made for their own enjoyment.  I criticize games I play constantly.  BUT the game dev demographic is a tiny minority.  If you want to make games for game devs, feel free.  You will struggle to sell them I think.

replies.author: Only-Cheetah-9579
replies.body: I agree that game devs are picky. But Im talking about AI in 10-15 years, it will be much more capable than today and playing a new game will be as easy as selecting a new movie on netflix

replies.author: Coldfriction
replies.body: I don't think you're going to get away from the energy costs that soon.  We'd need a different sort of AI on different hardware.

replies.author: Only-Cheetah-9579
replies.body: I agree, but the improvements are happening so fast that's always possible.

replies.author: Coldfriction
replies.body: The AI is improving fast, but the energy costs aren't so much.  It still costs thousands of dollars in tokens to make something good right now and token costs are below the AI provider costs currently.  They're all losing money at the current price points they sell tokens.

replies.author: Only-Cheetah-9579
replies.body:
Templating makes costs lower.

Its entirely possible to create a game but leave parts for later generation.

Some kids under 18 get a censored version.

Maybe somebody wants a black protagonist or a chinese one.

Maybe they want the game to have a different language or to take place elsewhere.

Somebody might like a more horror themed scary game while others want more story telling.

They all play the same game but the customizations are generated for them.

So it doesn't costs thousands. If the templating is good then generating a new protagonist can cost $1 , because the LLM just works with predictable templates.

comments.author: Ok-Ninja-8165
comments.body: But I do not want personalized custom game. I want game that is made by somebody with good vision.
